answer: Behavioral Cost Fingerprinting. Each identity’s outgoing transactions are sampled into a rolling shape vector; accounts that later behave like a river of clones are flagged by cross-correlation clustering. Enforcement: flagged clusters lose queue priority, and every member must pass a gale of fresh interaction challenges before regaining standing. Attacker cost: maintaining distinct timing and counterparty patterns across an ocean of agents, plus repeated challenge cycles per identity.
